title: Strict relative lifting after hypercover refinement for local acyclic fibrations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves.

Write $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$. A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets whose terms are small coproducts of representables and whose augmented matching maps become epimorphisms after sheafification. The degree-zero matching presheaf is $h_T$; all higher matching presheaves, parametrizing compatible proper faces, are formed in presheaves. A refinement over $T$ means a morphism of augmented simplicial presheaves over $h_T$. A collection is dense if every hypercover over every $T$ admits a refinement by a member of that collection over the same $T$.

Use simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. A simplicial presheaf is a functor $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$, and $h_T$ is regarded as a discrete simplicial presheaf. Write $\Delta^n$ for the represented standard simplex, $\partial\Delta^n$ for its boundary (empty for $n=0$), and $\Lambda_i^n$ for the union of all faces except face $i$, where $n\ge1$ and $0\le i\le n$. An objectwise Kan simplicial presheaf takes values in simplicial sets with fillers for every horn. A map $f:F\to G$ is a local Kan fibration if every commutative square from $h_V\times\Lambda_i^n\to h_V\times\Delta^n$ to $f$ has fillers after restriction along every arrow in some covering sieve of $V$; the fillers need not agree for different arrows of that sieve. For objectwise Kan $F,G$, call $f$ a local weak equivalence if it induces an isomorphism on the associated sheaves of $\pi_0$ and, for each $V\in\mathcal C$, $x\in F(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, on the associated sheaves on $\mathcal C/V$ of $\pi_m(F|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(G|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$. The slice topology is induced by covering sieves.

Let $F,G$ be objectwise Kan simplicial presheaves and let $f:F\to G$ be both a local Kan fibration and a local weak equivalence. Let $U_\bullet\to h_T$ be any hypercover, let $i:K\hookrightarrow L$ be an inclusion of simplicial sets with finitely many nondegenerate simplices (allowing $K=\varnothing$), and let $a:K\times U_\bullet\to F$ and $b:L\times U_\bullet\to G$ satisfy $f a=b(i\times1)$. Then there are a hypercover $V_\bullet\to h_T$, a refinement $v:V_\bullet\to U_\bullet$ over $h_T$, and a simplicial-presheaf map $\ell:L\times V_\bullet\to F$ satisfying the strict equations
$$\ell(i\times1)=a(1\times v),\qquad f\ell=b(1\times v).$$
Products with simplicial sets are computed objectwise. All hypercover matching objects and refinement morphisms are formed in presheaves.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Proposition 5.1 (diagram (5.2), conclusion (5.3)) and proof via Proposition 5.5, printed pp. 13-14; specialized to objectwise Kan F,G. Local acyclic fibrations are defined in Section 3, pp. 6-8. Read online; archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this arbitrary-site simplicial-presheaf lifting theorem.

proof.text: Put $H=F^L$ and $B=F^K\times_{G^K}G^L$. At $V\in\mathcal C$, currying a simplicial map $K\times U(V)\to F(V)$ gives the map $U(V)\to F(V)^K$, whose value on a $q$-simplex is its restriction to $K\times\Delta^q$. This is natural in $V$ and in simplicial operators, so $a,b$ define $c:U\to B$; the equation $fa=b(i\times1)$ is exactly the pullback condition. An $H$-valued lift of $c$ on a refinement is therefore the required $L$-valued tensor lift.

source.place: Proposition 5.1, proof: tensor-cotensor reformulation; objectwise tensor and cotensor formulas in Section 2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-hypercover-cotensor-local-acyclic-fibration] to $f$ and the finite inclusion $i$. It gives a local Kan fibration and local weak equivalence $p:H\to B$ with objectwise Kan $H,B$. Apply [lem-cbc-local-acyclic-matching-generalized-cover] to $p$: for every $m\ge0$, the relative boundary map $H_m\to\widetilde M_mH\times_{\widetilde M_mB}B_m$ is a generalized cover [def-cbc-generalized-cover]. Thus prescribed compatible faces in $H$, together with a compatible simplex in $B$, admit a strict simplex lift on a covering sieve.

source.place: Propositions 3.2 and 3.3, equation (3.4), and proof of Proposition 5.1.

proof.text: Use formal families [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct] and realize $\{A_j\}$ as $\coprod_j h_{A_j}$. A map from $h_A$ to such a coproduct is determined by its value at $\operatorname{id}_A$, a unique pair $(j,A\to A_j)$; restriction determines every other value. Hence formal-family maps are exactly maps between the realized presheaves. We construct split truncations: their degree-$q$ indices have unique labels $(\sigma,j)$, with $\sigma:[q]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ and $j$ a chosen nondegenerate index in degree $r$, and the component object is that at $j$.

source.place: Proposition 5.5, construction with new summands and degenerate summands; Section 4.12, split objects.

proof.text: Initialize in degree zero. For every $A\in\mathcal C$ and $t\in h_T(A)$, the hypercover condition and [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts] give a covering sieve $R_t$ on $A$ and sections $u_r\in U_0(D)$ above $t|_D$ for $r:D\to A$ in $R_t$. The degree-zero case of the relative boundary covers in Step 2 gives a covering sieve $S_{t,r}$ on $D$ and vertices $y_{r,s}\in H_0(E)$ with $p(y_{r,s})=c(u_r)|_E$ for $s:E\to D$ in $S_{t,r}$. Let $V_0$ be the coproduct of $h_E$ indexed by all these choices, with maps $v_0=u_r|_E$, $d_0=y_{r,s}$, and augmentation $t|_E$. The sieve of arrows along which $t$ lifts to $V_0$ covers: its pullback along each $r$ contains $S_{t,r}$, so transitivity applies to $R_t$. The reverse direction of the cited criterion makes $V_0^\#\to h_T^\#$ epic. Taking all these summands nondegenerate gives a split zero-truncation, and $pd_0=cv_0$ by its defining equation.

source.place: Lemma 5.4 and the initialization of the induction proving Proposition 5.1; the two covering sieves are composed using transitivity.

proof.text: Inductively assume a split $n$-truncated hypercover $V\to h_T$, a refinement $v:V\to U$ and a map $d:V\to H$ with $pd=cv$ through degree $n$. Put $m=n+1$ and let $M=M_m(V/h_T)$ be the presheaf of compatible proper faces over $h_T$ (for $m=1$, $M=V_0\times_{h_T}V_0$). Applying $v$ to each face gives $M\to M_m(U/h_T)$. For each $b\in M(A)$, [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts] applied to the matching map of $U$ supplies a covering sieve $R_b$ and simplices $u_r\in U_m(D)$ with boundary $v(b|_D)$ for $r:D\to A$ in it. The faces $d(b|_D)$ and the simplex $c(u_r)$ give a section of $\widetilde M_mH\times_{\widetilde M_mB}B_m$, since $pd=cv$ on every face. By Step 2, on a covering sieve $S_{b,r}$ of $D$ choose $y_{r,s}\in H_m(E)$ with boundary $d(b|_E)$ and $p(y_{r,s})=c(u_r)|_E$. Define $Z=\coprod_{A,b,r,s}h_E$, with boundary $b|_E$, map to $U_m$ given by $u_r|_E$, and map to $H_m$ given by $y_{r,s}$. All indices form a small set. For each $b$, the lifting sieve for $Z\to M$ pulls back along each $r$ to a sieve containing $S_{b,r}$; transitivity makes it covering. Thus $Z\to M$ is a generalized cover [def-cbc-generalized-cover], hence epic after sheafification by the cited criterion.

source.place: Proposition 5.5 and Lemma 5.4: relative matching pullback, with choices explicitly indexed by sections and composite sieve arrows.

proof.text:
The boundary maps of $Z$ to the lower $V_q$ form a compatible formal-family cone, by Step 3 and the definition of $M$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-split-attachment-operators] to this cone and the split truncation. It extends $V$ strictly with top degree
$$V_m=Z\amalg\coprod_{r\le n,\,\sigma:[m]\twoheadrightarrow[r]}N_r,$$
where $N_r$ is the nondegenerate family in degree $r$. Its normalized proper-epi formulas and invertible components are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-site-split-attachment-split], so the new truncation is split. On $Z$ define the maps to $U_m,H_m$ by Step 5; on $(\sigma,j)$ define them by $U(\sigma)v_r$ and $H(\sigma)d_r$ restricted to $N_{r,j}$. For a lower operator $\alpha:[q]\to[m]$, the new-summand equations are the chosen boundary equations. On an old summand, functoriality gives $U(\alpha)U(\sigma)v_r=U(\sigma\alpha)v_r=v_qV(\sigma\alpha)$, and the identical equation with $H,d$ gives its compatibility. For a proper epi from top degree to an old degree, both composites use the concatenated normalized label; its old component isomorphism cancels the inverse normalization. Factoring any ordinal map into an epi followed by a face inclusion verifies every remaining naturality equation, including nonidentity top endomorphisms. The augmentations agree because every boundary is over $h_T$. The equality $pd=cv$ holds on $Z$ by construction and on old summands by its lower-degree equality and naturality of $p,c$. Finally the matching map contains $Z\to M$ as a summand, so each section of $M$ lifts on the same covering sieve; [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts] makes the new matching map epic after sheafification. This proves the successor case of the inductive claim.

source.place: Proposition 5.5, final construction; explicit split attachment supplies degeneracies, and boundary equations verify both maps.

proof.text: Choose the stages successively. Define each term $V_q$ and every operator between degrees $q,r$ using a stage at least $\max(q,r)$; strict agreement with each preceding truncation makes these definitions independent of the stage. Every identity, composition, augmentation, and naturality equation occurs in a finite stage, where it has already been checked. Each matching map also occurs in a finite stage and is epic after sheafification. The resulting $V\to h_T$ is consequently a hypercover, with refinement $v:V\to U$ and map $d:V\to H$ satisfying $pd=cv$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.1, induction using Proposition 5.5; explicit assembly of the compatible truncations.

proof.text: Uncurry $d:V\to F^L$ objectwise to obtain $\ell:L\times V\to F$. Its projections under $p$ are precisely the restrictions of $a$ and $b$ along $v$, so $\ell(i\times1)=a(1\times v)$ and $f\ell=b(1\times v)$ as equalities of maps. Empty $K$ and degree-zero boundary cause no change to these formulas: $F^{\varnothing}$ is terminal, and Step 4 uses the empty boundary.

proof_origin.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen Proposition 5.1 and proof via Proposition 5.5, with Proposition 3.3 and Lemma 5.4.
